newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Armed men seize six people near Chechnya - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Armed men seize six people near Chechnya - Tass.

text.p: Armed men seized six people, five of them Chechens, as they travelled in a minibus near Russia's separatist region of Chechnya on Tuesday, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass quoted regional security officials as saying the six were travelling from the Caucasus region of North Ossetia to neighbouring Ingushetia, a few kilometres (miles) from the border with Chechnya. A spokeswoman at Russia's Emergencies Ministry said authorities were checking the report.
Tass gave no further details about the identity of the hostages.

Hostage-taking has become a major problem in Chechnya, where Russian troops fought a bloody campaign against separatist forces for 21 months until last August, but kidnappings are rare in neighbouring regions.

Last week, two British aid workers were seized from the house where they were staying in Chechnya by masked gunmen. Russian and foreign journalists and officials from the nearby Ingushetia and Ossetia regions have been among those kidnapped in Chechnya in recent months and some remain in captivity.
Chechen authorities said on Monday they were setting up a special mobile investigative unit, including judges of Islamic Sharia law, to tackle kidnappings in the region.
